answer: Each identity locks a 60-credit walnut bond and posts a self-assessed price on a terrace board in a sonnet declaration. Any challenger may buy it at that price, evicting the holder; resale within one epoch burns the bond. Auditors scan the cheapest terrace, so a low-priced fake is bought out fast, while a high-priced fake locks more capital. The kth fake needs its own bond and price: 1,000 fakes lock at least 60,000 credits. A rented identity fails because the buyout buyer owns the key. An honest agent posts one price, holds one bond, and reclaims it after a clean epoch.
